questions.sectionHeading: Section I (25 marks). Allow about 1 hour for this section.
questions.stem: To what extent can historians be certain about the past? Integrate Sources A and B and at least ONE other source throughout your argument.
questions.stimulus:
Source A: an extract from Katie Engelhart, "History on Trial", BBC History Magazine, 2013. The extract is copyright and is not reproduced here; read it in the 2021 HSC History Extension paper: https://www.nsw.gov.au/sites/default/files/noindex/2025-05/2021-hsc-history-extension.pdf

Source B: an extract from Richard J Evans, "Postmodernism and History", 22 October 2002, from the Great Debate on History and Postmodernism, University of New South Wales. The extract is copyright and is not reproduced here; read it in the 2021 HSC History Extension paper: https://www.nsw.gov.au/sites/default/files/noindex/2025-05/2021-hsc-history-extension.pdf
assessedOn: demonstrate knowledge and understanding of relevant issues of historiography
use relevant sources to support your argument
present a comprehensive, logical and sustained response

criteria.text: Provides a critical judgement on the extent to which historians can be certain about the past ; Supports argument with integrated and explicit references to Sources A and B, and at least ONE other relevant source ; Demonstrates extensive knowledge, complex understanding of, and critical insight into, relevant historiographical issues raised in Sources A and B ; Constructs a cohesive, logical and sustained response

Provides an effective judgement on the extent to which historians can be certain about the past ; Supports argument with explicit references to Sources A and B, and at least ONE other relevant source ; Demonstrates thorough knowledge and clear understanding of relevant historiographical issues raised in Sources A and B ; Constructs a logical and sustained response

Provides some judgement on the extent to which historians can be certain about the past ; Makes references to Sources A and B, and at least ONE other relevant source ; Demonstrates sound knowledge and understanding of historiographical issues raised in Sources A and/or B ; Constructs a clear response

Provides a limited discussion on the extent to which historians can be certain about the past ; Makes limited reference to Sources A and B and possibly ONE other relevant source ; Demonstrates limited knowledge and understanding of historiographical issues ; Presents a limited response

Provides isolated observations about historians and the past ; Makes minimal reference to Sources A and/or B and possibly ONE other relevant source ; Demonstrates minimal knowledge of historiographical issues

questions.sectionHeading: Section II (25 marks). Allow about 1 hour for this section.
questions.stem: Evaluate the influence of context in the construction of historical interpretations. In your response, refer to Source C and at least ONE area of debate in your case study. Identify your case study at the beginning of your answer.
questions.stimulus: [Source C: a cartoon, ©2010 baloocartoons.com. The cartoon is copyright and is not reproduced here; read it in the 2021 HSC History Extension paper: https://www.nsw.gov.au/sites/default/files/noindex/2025-05/2021-hsc-history-extension.pdf. Description: two figures in animal-skin clothing stand at the left. The figure at the left says, in a speech bubble, 'DON'T BELIEVE EVERYTHING YOU READ.' At the right, a seated figure holds a stick to a rock wall, with a smaller figure beside it. On the wall is a drawing of an elephant with a long trunk, and an arrow drawn on the wall points at the elephant. The caption reads '©2010 baloocartoons.com'.]
assessedOn: demonstrate knowledge and understanding of an appropriate case study
engage with the historiography of the areas of debate selected for discussion
present a comprehensive, logical and sustained response

criteria.text: Provides a critical evaluation of the influence of context in the construction of historical interpretations ; Supports argument(s) with explicit references to Source C and at least ONE area of debate in their chosen case study ; Demonstrates extensive knowledge, complex understanding of, and critical insight into, historiographical issues from the chosen area(s) of debate in their case study ; Constructs a cohesive, logical and sustained response

Provides an effective evaluation of the influence of context in the construction of historical interpretations ; Supports argument(s) with references to Source C and at least ONE area of debate in their chosen case study ; Demonstrates thorough knowledge and clear understanding of historiographical issues from the chosen area(s) of debate in their case study ; Constructs a logical and sustained response

Provides some evaluation of the influence of context and the construction of historical interpretations ; Makes references to Source C and at least ONE area of debate in their chosen case study ; Demonstrates sound knowledge and understanding of historiographical issues from the chosen area(s) of debate in their case study ; Constructs a clear response

Provides a description about context and historical interpretations ; Makes limited reference to Source C and/or at least ONE area of debate in their chosen case study ; Demonstrates limited knowledge and/or understanding of historiographical issues from the chosen area(s) of debate in their case study ; Presents a limited response

Provides isolated observations about context and/or historical interpretation(s) ; May make reference to Source C and/or ONE area of debate in their chosen case study ; Demonstrates minimal knowledge of the chosen area(s) of debate in their case study
